theater: 米蘭公國與倫巴第波河下游

battle.name: 第六次意大利戰爭
battle.theater: 米蘭公國與倫巴第波河下游
battle.brief: 一五二一年五月法王弗朗索瓦一世遣軍越阿爾卑斯山入米蘭公國，戰爭爆發；法軍先取米蘭、圍帕維亞，一五二二年二月卻在比科卡敗北。一五二四年波旁再率大軍圍那不勒斯，二五年二月二十四日帕維亞野戰中被西班牙-帝國軍夜襲破陣，弗朗索瓦被生擒。火槍線仍以火繩步槍為骨幹，輪發手槍只配軍官與近衛。

kit.name: 輪發槍
kit.history: 最早的後膛手槍。機械太貴，只給火槍隊的軍官與衛兵。

countries:
此役的交戰方是法王弗朗索瓦一世一方，與神聖羅馬帝國皇帝卡爾五世（兼西班牙國王卡洛斯一世）一方。一五二〇年代前半的義大利並無統一國家，雙方的軍隊都由王室常備兵、外來傭兵與義大利同盟拼湊而成。
法國一側的骨幹是十二支「秩序連隊」，每連約一百五十人，另有王家重砲隊、王室騎兵連，以及一支以手槍為主要武器的近衛連（pistoliers du roi）；最後這支連隊正是最有可能配發輪發手槍的編制。弗朗索瓦一世支持的朱利奧·德·梅迪奇於一五二三年當選教宗後，意大利聯盟成立，計有威尼斯共和國、教宗國、佛羅倫薩、米蘭（斯福爾扎家族的弗朗切斯科二世）與熱那亞（安德烈亞·多里亞），一五二四年起聯盟部隊與法軍併肩作戰。法軍另大量僱用德意志蘭斯克內希特長矛兵與火槍手、薩爾茨堡射擊兵、意大利合閘手槍手，並有瑞士傭兵團若干；軍中僱傭兵欠餉與紀律問題屢見不鮮。
帝國—西班牙一側以西班牙老兵方陣為核心，輔以德意志傭兵與帝國各地徵召的騎兵，義大利方面由科隆那、佩斯卡拉、拉努瓦等經驗老到的傭兵隊長率領當地部隊；教宗國初期站在皇帝一方，一五二四年後倒向法國。帝國軍配備攻城重砲與火繩步槍，並有口徑極大的「使徒」級巨砲可用於攻堅。戰區之外，匈牙利—土耳其前線、帝國腹地的德意志宗教衝突（一五二一年沃爾姆斯帝國會議、一五二四至二五年的農民戰爭）都抽走了可用於義大利的德意志傭兵，逼得雙方都想速戰速決。
countriesEn: The belligerents on this theatre are Francis I of France on one side and the Emperor Charles V, who is also King Carlos I of Spain, on the other. In the first half of the 1520s Italy was not a single country, and the armies of both sides were patched together from royal household troops, foreign mercenaries and Italian allies. The backbone of the French army was the twelve companies of the ordering, each of about a hundred and fifty men, together with the royal heavy artillery park, the royal cavalry companies, and a bodyguard unit whose main weapon was the pistol, the pistoliers du roi; that last unit is precisely where a wheellock pistol was most likely to be issued. After Giulio de' Medici was elected pope in 1523 with Francis I's backing, the Italian League was formed, comprising the republic of Venice, the Papal States, Florence, Milan under Francesco II Sforza and Genoa under Andrea Doria, and from 1524 League troops fought alongside the French army. The French also hired large numbers of German Landsknecht pikemen and shot, Salzburg shooters, Italian arquebusiers of the combined calibre, and several companies of Swiss mercenaries; arrears of pay and discipline problems among these hired soldiers recur again and again in the sources. The imperial-Spanish side was built around the veteran Spanish tercios, supported by German mercenaries and cavalry levied in the empire, while in Italy the campaign was led by experienced condottieri such as Colonna, Pescara and Lannoy. The Papal States at first stood with the emperor and turned to France only after 1524. The imperial train carried siege cannon and matchlock muskets, together with very large bore guns of the Apostles class for siege work. Beyond the theatre itself, the Hungarian-Turkish front and the religious conflict in the German lands, including the Diet of Worms in 1521 and the Peasants' War of 1524-25, drained away the German mercenaries available for service in Italy, so that both sides wanted a quick decision.
people:
此役的關鍵人物集中在法王、帝國統帥與教宗三方。
法國方面：一五二一年五月率軍越過阿爾卑斯山入義大利的是拉烏特雷克子爵（奧德·德·福瓦）與塔爾蒙親王路易二世·德·拉·特雷穆瓦，兩人率約兩萬人奪取米蘭、圍困帕維亞；拉烏特雷克於同年十二月二十二日卒於軍中疫病，特雷穆瓦亦在圍城期間斃命，接掌法軍的福瓦在比科卡再敗陣亡。一五二四年再入義大利的法軍，實際在場統率的是聖波爾伯爵弗朗索瓦·德·波旁；掌法國軍務的Constable是波旁第三公，但他自一五二三年在納瓦拉被俘後一直囚於西班牙，直到一五二六年才獲釋，並未上陣。這支部隊進軍米蘭、圍攻那不勒斯，同行的還有阿朗松公爵與內穆爾公爵。一五二五年帕維亞之役，法軍的戰場指揮由聖波爾伯爵、阿朗松公爵與內穆爾公爵在前線統籌，王室重砲隊由砲兵總監博韋率領。
帝國方面：那不勒斯總督拉努瓦是全軍總指揮，佩斯卡拉侯爵費蘭特·德·阿瓦洛斯是最鋒利的突擊手，萊瓦統帶西班牙步兵，戰後出任米蘭總督；一五二四年奉卡爾五世之命把西班牙老兵運抵熱那亞的是萊雷納伯爵費爾南多·阿爾瓦雷斯·德·托萊多。佩斯卡拉侯爵在帕維亞受重傷，二月二十六日傷重去世，戰功大半記在他名下。
其他人：教宗朱利奧·德·梅迪奇在法國與帝國之間來回轉向，決定了意大利聯盟的成立與崩解；熱那亞海軍統帥安德烈亞·多里亞先為法國作戰，一五二八年才轉投皇帝。法軍陣亡的巴亞爾元帥是全役最被後世記住的兵將之一，他的死與國王的被俘一起成為此役的象徵。
peopleEn: The decisive personalities of this war cluster around the French king, the imperial commanders and the pope. On the French side: the men who led the army over the Alps into Italy in May 1521 were the Viscount of Lautrec, Odet de Foix, and Louis II de la Tre'mouille, Prince of Talmont, who took Milan and then ringed Pavia with some twenty thousand men; Lautrec died of sickness in the camp on 22 December 1521, Tre'mouille also died during that siege, and Foix, who took over command, was killed at Bicocca the following year. The army that invaded Italy again in 1524 was led on the ground by Franpois de Bourbon, Count of Saint-Pol; the Constable of the French host was Charles, Duke of Bourbon, but he had been captured in Navarre in 1523 and stayed a prisoner in Spain until his release in 1526, so he never took the field. That army entered Milan and laid siege to Naples, with the Duke of Alencon and the Duke of Nemours alongside. At Pavia in 1525 the field command on the French side was in the hands of the Count of Saint-Pol, the Duke of Alencon and the Duke of Nemours, with the royal heavy artillery led by the master of the ordnance, Bovee. On the imperial side: Charles de Lannoy, viceroy of Naples, commanded the whole army; the Marquis of Pescara, Ferrante d'Avalos, was the sharpest of the assault commanders; Leyva led the Spanish foot and afterwards became governor of Milan; and the Count of Lerena, Fernando Alvarez de Toledo, was the man Charles V sent to bring the Spanish veterans to Genoa in 1524. Pescara was badly wounded at Pavia and died of his wounds on 26 February, and most of the credit for the victory is written against his name. Others: Pope Giulio de' Medici swung back and forth between France and the Empire, and his turns decided the making and the breaking of the Italian League; the Genoese admiral Andrea Doria served France first and did not defect to the emperor until 1528. The French marshal Bayard, who fell in the fighting, is the soldier of this war most remembered afterwards, and his death together with the capture of the king became the emblem of Pavia.
kits:
此役的裝備骨架是長矛、火繩步槍（archibuse）、重砲與騎兵火器。義大利與西班牙的步兵主力仍是火繩槍手：西班牙方陣以火繩手槍配支架，彈藥用皮帶分裝成多個分裝包，裝填慢而怕雨；法軍與聯盟軍同樣以火繩步槍為主，並大量使用合閘手槍與輕型步槍。長矛手與火槍手的比例、旗手與軍旗排面仍按早期方陣的辦法配置，攻城則靠數十門重砲與「使徒」級大口徑巨砲。
卡面這件輪發手槍在此役的位置相當明確：輪發機構是十五世紀末到十六世紀初在低地國家與德意志出現的後膛發火機件，靠上弦的發條帶動鋼輪撞擊火石，毋須火繩，但每次上弦要轉動多圈，機件怕潮、耗藥多、造價遠高於火繩手槍。萊昂納多·達·文西的《大西洋手稿》正是同一時期記錄了這種名為「pistola dephere」的機構。因而在一五二一到二五年的義大利戰場上，步兵火線仍然是火繩步槍，輪發手槍主要落在三種人手上：連隊與中隊的軍官及侍從、王室近衛（法國的pistoliers與西班牙的guardia），以及需要下馬步戰的騎兵軍官；用途是近身自衛、對付衝到面前的落馬騎士與散兵，並在夜戰之中不受火繩的限制而隨時可用。帕維亞是夜戰又是雨戰，這一點特別要緊。
其餘裝備：法國重騎用甲冑、長柄騎槍與刺馬槍，帝國方陣配長柄斧矛與雙手劍，輕騎用火繩手槍配輕盔；運輸與後勤靠騾車隊與可拆式浮橋，攻城與行軍的糧秣、彈藥全靠牛騾馱運，而這正是法軍在帕維亞敗陣的重要原因之一。
kitsEn: The equipment skeleton of this war is the pike, the matchlock musket, heavy artillery and mounted firearms. The infantry mass of Italy and Spain remained matchlock gunners: the Spanish tercios fired matchlock arquebuses rested on supports, with the ammunition carried in bandoliers divided into several charges, slow to load and afraid of rain; the French and League armies relied on matchlock muskets in the same way and used large numbers of combined calibre arquebuses and lighter muskets. The ratio of pikemen to shot, the position of the ensigns and the order of the regimental colours still followed the older tercio practice, and siege work was done with dozens of heavy guns together with very large bore pieces of the Apostles class. The position of the wheellock pistol on the card is quite precise: the wheel-lock mechanism is a breech ignition device that appeared in the Low Countries and in Germany at the end of the fifteenth and the beginning of the sixteenth century, driving a steel wheel from a wound spring to strike against pyrite, and needing no burning match; but it takes many turns of the crank to cock, the mechanism suffers from damp, it burns a lot of powder, and it costs far more than a matchlock gun. Leonardo da Vinci's Codex Atlanticus records a mechanism of exactly this kind in the same decade, under the name of the pistola dephere. So on the Italian battlefields of 1521 to 1525 the infantry firing line was still matchlock, and the wheellock pistol fell mainly into the hands of three sorts of men: captains and officers of companies, the bodyguard of princes and captains, on the French side the pistoliers and on the Spanish side the guardia, and mounted officers who had to fight on foot. Its uses were personal protection in close fighting, dealing with knights unhorsed in the melee and with scattered fugitives, and being usable at any moment in night fighting without the constraint of a burning match. Pavia was fought at night and in rain, and that is exactly where this mattered. The rest of the equipment: French heavy horse in armour with long lances and couched coubardes, imperial foot with long-handled halberds and two-handed swords, light horse with matchlock arquebuses and light helmets; transport and supply depended on mule trains and demountable pontoon bridges, and the grain, ammunition and siege train of a marching army moved on oxen and mules, which was one of the chief reasons the French lost at Pavia.
tactics:
一五二一年法軍的戰法是速決：拉烏特雷克先取米蘭，再與威尼斯、教宗援軍會合，把帝國—西班牙聯軍逐出米蘭，然後圍帕維亞。但科隆那與佩斯卡拉率領的解圍軍採取夜行與野地築壘的辦法，避開法軍鋒頭，一度切斷帕維亞與米蘭之間的聯繫；拉烏特雷克死於疫病後，圍城解體。
比科卡是此役第一個戰術樣本：一五二二年二月二十三日，科隆那把聯軍佈在米蘭以北的比科卡高地上，前面利用一條水道（fosso）作天然壕溝，砲位居高臨下；法軍不待援軍到齊就正面強攻，隊形在泥濘中拉成散亂的縱隊，缺砲兵掩護，衝進水道的人大量溺斃，天亮時聯軍反擊，法軍崩潰。經此一敗，法軍在此後三年不敢再碰有備的野戰。
一五二四年法軍轉取圍城：聖波爾伯爵率聯軍渡過米蘭，圍困那不勒斯；卡爾五世把西班牙老兵由海路運到熱那亞，與拉努瓦、佩斯卡拉、萊瓦的帝國軍會合，沿波河谷南下，於一五二五年二月下旬逼近帕維亞。帕維亞之役本身就是一場夜戰：二月二十三日入夜暴雨不停，法軍冒雨夜行出營，砲車陷在泥中無法推進；法軍騎兵先衝帝國軍的側翼，步兵在稻田與葡萄園之間的窄地展開，射界不足；帝國軍以德意志與西班牙步兵居中、火槍手列於兩翼高處，穩守待戰，待法軍縱隊走完才反擊。法軍潰散時，帕維亞城堡的守軍開砲掩射，退路被切斷，國王本人腿部中火槍彈，與大批隨員被俘。輪發手槍正是在夜戰與泥濘這一段最有價值：不必舉著火繩，不怕火繩被雨澆滅，軍官與近衛可以一邊上弦一邊自衛；代價是上弦緩慢、機件怕潮，必須預備上弦匙。
tacticsEn: The French plan of 1521 was a quick decision: Lautrec was to take Milan first, join the reinforcements from Venice and the Papal States, drive the imperial-Spanish league out of Milan, and then invest Pavia. But the relief army of Colonna and Pescara used night marches and field entrenchments to avoid the French thrust and at one point cut the link between Pavia and Milan; after Lautrec died of sickness the siege simply came apart. Bicocca is the first tactical lesson of the war: on 23 February 1522 Colonna drew the league army up on the heights of Bicocca north of Milan, using a watercourse as a natural ditch in front and placing the guns above to command the ground. The French attacked head on without waiting for their reinforcements; in the mud their formation drew out into disordered columns, they had no artillery cover, and those who charged into the watercourse were drowned in large numbers. At daylight the league counter-attacked and the French army broke. After that reverse the French did not attempt a prepared field battle for three years. In 1524 the French turned to siege warfare: the army of Saint-Pol crossed into Milan and invested Naples; Charles V brought the Spanish veterans by sea to Genoa, where they joined the imperial troops of Lannoy, Pescara and Leyva, and moved down the Po valley to reach Pavia in late February 1525. Pavia itself was a night battle: rain poured down through the night of 23 February as the French marched out of camp, their gun carriages sank into the mud and could not be moved forward, the French horse charged the flank of the imperial line, and the foot was deployed in the narrow ground between rice fields and vineyards with far too little room to shoot. The imperial-Spanish army kept German and Spanish foot in the centre with the arquebusiers posted on the higher ground of both wings, stood fast, and counter-attacked only when the French columns had walked themselves out. When the French broke, the garrison of the castle of Pavia opened fire and cut the road back, the king was struck in the leg by an arquebus ball, and he and a great many of his entourage were taken. The wheellock pistol was at its most valuable exactly in that night and mud: no match to hold alight, no fear of the match being drowned, so officers and guards could cock and defend themselves at the same time. The price was slow cocking and a mechanism that hates damp, which meant carrying the winding key ready.
data:
可核對的數字集中在幾個節點。一五二一年法軍入義大利的總兵力約兩萬人，另有威尼斯與教宗方各一部。一五二二年二月二十三日比科卡之戰，法軍出動約兩萬至兩萬五千人，帝國—教宗—西班牙聯軍約八千至一萬人，其中瑞士傭兵約四千；法軍陣亡約四千人，許多人是在水道中溺斃，聯軍損失相對有限。
一五二四年再入義利的法軍連同聯盟軍約三萬至四萬人，圍那不勒斯自八月起。一五二五年二月二十四日帕維亞之戰，法軍野戰部隊約三萬人，連同圍城的瑞士與意大利營，總數在三萬上下，史料亦有高至三萬九千的說法；帝國—西班牙軍約兩萬至兩萬四千，其中德意志與西班牙步兵約一萬二千至一萬四千、騎兵約四千至八千。帝國軍自米蘭南下至帕維亞，路程約一百三十至一百六十公里，走了近三個月，說明這是一場計畫周密的遠征而非奔襲。戰鬥自二十三日夜間開始，二十四日凌晨分出勝負。法軍陣亡約八千至一萬二千人，被俘約八千至一萬人，國王、內穆爾公爵、阿朗松公爵與大批貴族在俘之列；帝國軍的損失以數百人計。帕維亞城堡在洛多維科·德·薩盧佐侯爵率領下固守至同年六月十日左右，以榮譽條款開城。
政治與財政的數字同樣重要：一五二六年一月二十二日《馬德里條約》規定法國放棄米蘭與那不勒斯、交付五十萬埃居，並以兩名王子作人質，這筆錢最終談到一百萬埃居；同年八月卡爾五世向富格爾家族籌得約十五萬達克的借款，用來發放欠餉，而一五二六年三月弗朗索瓦一世獲釋返法。傷亡的精確數字在當時並不可靠，能確定的是法軍損失以萬計、國王被俘這兩件事本身。
dataEn: The verifiable figures cluster around a few dates. The French army that entered Italy in 1521 numbered about twenty thousand men, with a further contingent each from Venice and from the Papal side. At the battle of Bicocca on 23 February 1522 the French fielded roughly twenty to twenty-five thousand, against eight to ten thousand for the imperial-Papal-Spanish league, of whom about four thousand were Swiss mercenaries; some four thousand French were killed, many of them drowned in the watercourse, while the league losses were comparatively small. The French army that invaded Italy again in 1524, together with the League contingents, was about thirty to forty thousand strong, and the investment of Naples began in August. At Pavia on 24 February 1525 the French field army was about thirty thousand, or something near thirty thousand with the Swiss and Italian companies still besieging the city, though some sources give as many as thirty-nine thousand; the imperial-Spanish army was about twenty to twenty-four thousand, of which twelve to fourteen thousand were German and Spanish foot and four to eight thousand horse. The imperial force covered something like one hundred and thirty to one hundred and sixty kilometres from Milan down to Pavia in close to three months, which shows a carefully planned march of the army rather than a rush. The fighting began during the night of the 23rd and was decided in the small hours of the 24th. The French lost some eight to twelve thousand dead and eight to ten thousand prisoners, among them the king, the Duke of Nemours, the Duke of Alencon and a great many of the nobility; the imperial-Spanish losses are counted in the hundreds. The castle of Pavia, held by the Marquis Ludovico of Saluzzo, resisted until about 10 June of the same year and then opened on honourable terms. The political and financial figures matter just as much: the Treaty of Madrid of 22 January 1526 required France to abandon Milan and Naples, to pay five hundred thousand ecus and to send two of the princes to Spain as hostages, and the sum was later negotiated up to one million ecus; in August of the same year Charles V borrowed about one hundred and fifty thousand ducats from the Fugger family to pay his arrears, and in March 1526 Francis I was released and returned to France. Exact casualty figures are not reliable at this distance, but two things are certain: French losses in the tens of thousands, and the capture of the king.
cause:
一五二一年開戰的根源是米蘭。義大利戰爭打了四分之一個世紀，弗朗索瓦一世把米蘭視為法國的門戶，一五一六年《努瓦松條約》把米蘭公國交給法國，並扶弗朗切斯科二世·斯福爾扎复位；卡爾五世在一五一九年當選皇帝、一五二一年即位西班牙國王之後，哈布斯堡與瓦洛瓦的宿怨就到了非分不可的地步：一五二一年四月法國高等法院宣稱凡與哈布斯堡所訂條約一概無效，而教宗與帝國的聯盟也早已破裂，新的教宗選舉尚未決定法國的處境。
雙方的直接爭執有三層。第一是米蘭本身的歸屬，卡爾五世不能容忍法國插手他打算用作通往布魯塞爾與西班牙的通道。第二是王位位階之爭，帝國方面要求歸還勃艮第。第三是教宗國的生存：朱利奧·德·梅迪奇既恨哈布斯堡的包圍，又怕法國利用米蘭作為跳板，於是他在一五二三年底站到法國一邊，意大利聯盟成立，戰爭的舞台由米蘭擴展到那不勒斯。
弗朗索瓦一世決定在一五二一年先發制人，因為米蘭一旦落入哈布斯堡之手，法國在義大利的橋頭堡就會消失；他低估的是西班牙老兵方陣的成熟與帝國重砲的機動能力，也低估了德意志傭兵在薩爾茨堡一帶、在帕維亞一線能夠提供的人數。最後，戰爭在財政上拖垮了法國：帕維亞慘敗、國王被俘，意大利聯盟隨即瓦解，這一場戰爭的段落要等到一五二六年的《馬德里條約》才劃下句號。
causeEn: The root of the war that began in 1521 was Milan. The Italian Wars had already run for a quarter of a century, and Francis I regarded Milan as France's gateway; the Treaty of Noyon of 1516 handed the duchy of Milan to France and restored Francesco II Sforza to it. Once Charles V had been elected emperor in 1519 and had taken the Spanish crown in 1521, the Habsburg-Valois enmity reached the point where it could not be held any longer: in April 1521 the French Parlement declared all treaties made with the Habsburg null, the papal-imperial alliance had long since broken up, and the choice of a new pope had not yet settled France's position. There were three layers of direct dispute. The first was Milan itself, which Charles V could not tolerate in French hands because he meant it as a road to Brussels and Spain. The second was the ranking of crowns, the imperial side demanding the restitution of Burgundy. The third was the survival of the Papal States: Giulio de' Medici hated the Habsburg encirclement but equally feared a France that used Milan as a springboard, so by the end of 1523 he had moved to the French side, the Italian League was formed, and the stage of the war widened from Milan to Naples. Francis I decided to strike first in 1521 because if Milan fell to the Habsburg the French bridgehead in Italy would disappear. What he underestimated was the maturity of the Spanish veteran tercios, the mobility of the imperial heavy artillery, and the number of German mercenaries that could be raised around Salzburg and on the line towards Pavia. In the end the war ruined France financially: the defeat at Pavia and the capture of the king broke up the Italian League, and this particular round of the Italian Wars was not closed off until the Treaty of Madrid of 1526.
impact:
此役的影響遠超過它本身的勝負。第一，弗朗索瓦一世被俘在歐洲政治裏是一次地震式的衝擊：國王落在敵營的消息傳遍歐洲，繪畫與敘事把這件事寫成騎士價值的考驗，這種說法更可能是事後編造，但確實成了法國王室的資產，法國王位自此能以「受難者」身分自居。一五二六年的《馬德里條約》與一百萬埃居的贖金，把哈布斯堡在義大利的地位固定下來。
第二，軍事技術上，帕維亞被後世視為長矛與火槍戰術的轉折點：重騎的衝鋒無法衝散密集的長矛方陣與有掩體的火槍線，義大利戰場此後數十年不再出現大規模騎兵決戰，火槍手與長矛手的比例、旗手排面與火槍射擊的統一節奏，都從這幾年裡定型。第三，這場戰爭把西班牙老兵方陣推到歐洲軍事舞台中央，而方陣的長處恰恰是能吸收火繩槍的劣點：排水、快裝、靠陣形互相掩護，彌補裝填慢與怕雨。帝國軍隊裡的德意志傭兵自此成了各方爭搶的資源。
第四，帝國在義大利的控制力讓卡爾五世可以把重心轉向北方與地中海，匈牙利王路易二世於一五二六年陣亡，匈牙利王國隨即被奧斯曼吞併，帝國的資源為之吃緊；卡爾五世自一五二六年起組成的干邑聯盟，又把法國推回義大利，戰爭直接延續到一五三〇年才以《尼斯和約》與《巴塞羅那條約》收場。最後要記住的是人員的代價：帕維亞一役法軍陣亡以萬計，被俘者近萬，數千德意志與瑞士傭兵散落各國，這些人回到各自的營壘裡，就成了下一輪雇傭戰爭的燃料。
impactEn: The consequences of this war reach far beyond its own outcome. First, the captivity of Francis I was an earthquake in European politics: the news that a king was in the enemy's hands spread across Europe, and painting and narrative turned the event into a test of knightly honour. That reading is probably a later invention, but it did become an asset of the French crown, which from then on could present itself as the wronged party. The Treaty of Madrid of 1526 and the ransom of a million ecus fixed the Habsburg position in Italy. Second, in military technology Pavia came to be seen as the turning point of pike and shot: the charge of heavy horse could not break a dense pike block backed by covered arquebus fire, and for decades afterwards no large scale cavalry decision was fought on the Italian field; the ratio of pikemen to shot, the place of the ensigns, and the synchronised rhythm of the arquebus volleys were all fixed during these years. Third, the war pushed the veteran Spanish tercio to the centre of the European stage, and the strength of the tercio was precisely that it absorbed the weakness of the matchlock, namely its slow loading and its fear of rain, through discipline, quick drill and mutual cover from the formation itself. The German mercenaries in the imperial army became a resource that every side tried to hire. Fourth, control of Italy allowed Charles V to turn his attention north and to the Mediterranean: Louis II of Hungary fell at Mohacs in 1526, the kingdom was swallowed by the Ottomans, and the resources of the empire grew strained; the League of Cognac that Charles V faced from 1526 onward pushed France back into Italy, and the war ran on until 1530 before being wound up by the Treaty of Nice and the Treaty of Barcelona. The last point to keep in mind is the cost in men: the French lost tens of thousands dead at Pavia and close to ten thousand prisoners, and several thousand German and Swiss mercenaries were scattered back across Europe into the camps where they became the fuel of the next round of paid wars.
result:
一五二一年五月法軍取米蘭，九月圍帕維亞，同年十二月拉烏特雷克病歿、圍城解體，帝國—教宗聯軍收回米蘭。一五二二年二月二十三日比科卡，法軍再敗，損失約四千人，圍城的法軍退回法國，義大利戰線上只剩教宗國的態度未定。
一五二三年底教宗朱利奧·德·梅迪奇倒向法國，意大利聯盟成立。一五二四年聖波爾伯爵率聯軍入義大利，圍困那不勒斯；卡爾五世自西班牙派老兵增援，帝國軍沿波河谷南下。一五二五年二月二十四日帕維亞，法軍因夜襲大雨、砲車陷泥而失序，慘敗，國王被俘，一萬人左右被擄；同年六月十日帕維亞城堡以榮譽條款開城，圍那不勒斯之師隨之瓦解，那不勒斯王國歸帝國。
一五二六年一月二十二日《馬德里條約》：法國放棄米蘭與那不勒斯，交付五十萬埃居，兩名王子送往西班牙作人質，勃艮第的問題懸而未決。三月弗朗索瓦一世獲釋返法，拒絕承認條約的實質，於五月二十二日拉起干邑聯盟，戰爭直接延續到下一段。最後的結果是：義大利分成兩半，帝國與西班牙得米蘭與那不勒斯，法國退守本國，以後用二十多年時間再打回來。
resultEn: In May 1521 the French took Milan and in September invested Pavia; in December of the same year Lautrec died of sickness, the siege came apart, and the imperial-Papal league recovered Milan. At Bicocca on 23 February 1522 the French were beaten a second time, losing some four thousand men, and the besieging French withdrew to France, leaving only the attitude of the Papal States unsettled on the Italian front. At the end of 1523 Pope Giulio de' Medici turned to France and the Italian League was formed. In 1524 the army of Saint-Pol entered Italy and invested Naples; Charles V sent veterans from Spain as reinforcement and the imperial force moved down the Po valley. On 24 February 1525, at Pavia, the French lost their order in the night attack and in the rain, with the gun carriages stuck in the mud; they were destroyed, the king was taken, and about ten thousand men were carried off as prisoners. On 10 June of the same year the castle of Pavia opened on honourable terms, the army that had been besieging Naples fell apart, and the kingdom of Naples passed to the Empire. The Treaty of Madrid of 22 January 1526 required France to abandon Milan and Naples, to pay five hundred thousand ecus and to send two princes to Spain as hostages, leaving the question of Burgundy open. Francis I was released and returned to France in March, refused to accept the substance of the treaty, and on 22 May raised the League of Cognac, which carried the war straight into its next phase. The final result was that Italy was split in two: the Empire and Spain gained Milan and Naples, France fell back behind its own frontier, and would spend the next twenty years trying to fight its way back.
